text:
Application lifecycle

The application lifecycle is the continuous process of creating, delivering, operating, and improving an application, from the initial idea through eventual retirement.

1. Conception and discovery: Define the business problem, users, expected value, constraints, and success measures.
2. Requirements: Describe capabilities, workflows, data, integrations, security needs, and acceptance criteria.
3. Solution design: Design the user experience, architecture, data model, interfaces, and operational controls.
4. Planning: Prioritize scope, divide work into increments, estimate effort, assign ownership, and manage dependencies and risks.
5. Development: Build, configure, review, and document the application.
6. Testing: Validate functionality, integrations, security, accessibility, performance, and user acceptance.
7. Release and deployment: Approve and package a version, prepare support and rollback measures, and deploy it to production.
8. Operations: Monitor reliability, security, usage, and service levels while handling support, incidents, backups, and maintenance.
9. Continuous improvement: Use feedback, telemetry, and business results to identify and deliver improvements.
10. Retirement: When the application no longer provides sufficient value, migrate users and data, remove dependencies, and decommission it safely.

The lifecycle is iterative rather than strictly linear: testing can return work to development, operational findings can create new requirements, and continuous improvement begins another cycle.
